speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you're experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand what's happening, have these symptoms been present since you woke up this morning?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest is very suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty swallowing recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.
